verdict.rationale: Floot's own docs say you can export a project's code (a real TypeScript/React app) and its database, download a full SQL dump at any time on any plan, and self-host elsewhere. That covers both exporting in open formats and leaving. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the export flow, and documentation that platform-held data beyond code and database (analytics, email logs, uploaded assets, auth users) is also exportable.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: you can export the code and the database and deploy them wherever you like.
You can download a full SQL dump of your database at any time, on any plan
A Floot project is a real TypeScript and React app — pages, components, and backend endpoints — and you can read or export all of it.
you can browse the tables and download a backup yourself.
